scope: Same-sample validation comparison of the step-150 LoRA checkpoint and immutable public DROID base
summary: The 4.8828125e-4 step-150 adapter improved motion correlation but substantially degraded appearance and static consistency on both isolated validation episodes, so it is rejected for demos and further continuation.
evidence: Both methods independently generated ep012 and ep020 at 768x432, 16 fps, 93 frames with the same real first-frame conditions, prompt embeddings, negative embedding, seed 20260812, and guidance 7.
Condition-frame SSIM remained high and comparable: public base 0.977883 versus LoRA-150 0.976853.
LoRA-150 versus base deltas were mean full-frame SSIM -0.166347, subject edge F1 -0.199977, subject ROI SSIM -0.131816, and minimum full-frame SSIM -0.139936.
Motion correlation improved from 0.042949 to 0.227065 (+0.184116), but motion magnitude ratio worsened from 2.244277 to 2.847688.
Neither base nor LoRA-150 passed all strict gates; LoRA-150 output status is PARTIAL and is not eligible for demo promotion.
lessons: At rank 16, the original learning rate is too aggressive for appearance-preserving task adaptation even though it begins to learn temporal motion.
The next experiment should sweep much earlier checkpoints at a lower explicit learning rate and require base-relative appearance preservation before considering motion gains.
limitations: The validation set has two episodes; it is used for checkpoint selection only and no final-holdout claim is made.
Pixel-aligned metrics do not replace visual review, but the degradation is broad and large enough to reject this checkpoint before demo review.
next_actions: Train a fresh 1e-4 run with checkpoints at steps 25, 50, and 75; evaluate candidates against the same public-base validation outputs and stop any candidate that violates appearance-preservation constraints.
